newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's opposition Labour jumps to lead in TV3 poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ's opposition Labour jumps to lead in TV3 poll.

text.p: New Zealand's opposition Labour Party has jumped to a 15 point lead over the ruling National Party in the party ratings, according to a TV3/CM Research opinion poll published on Wednesday.

Compared to CM's last poll taken a week befor the October 12 election, the poll suggested large swings by voters to Labour from the left-wing Alliance Party and New Zealand First, National's coalition partner, rather than away from National whose support has held steady at 30 percent.
CM said Labour leader Helen Clark had become clear favourite as preferred prime minister with 25 percent support, 10 points ahead of National leader and incumbent Jim Bolger.
Support for NZ First leader and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters fell to four percent from 14 percent.
Sixty-three percent of the the 500 people polled disagreed with the idea of compulsory pensions, compared with 68 percent support for the concept in July 1996.
